# New-ZbxRegExp

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a global regular expression.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxRegExp [[-Name] <string>] [-TestString <string>] [-Expression <ZabbixRegExpExpressionRequest[]>] [-Description <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A global regular expression is a named set of expressions that log items, low-level discovery filters and other fields refer to as @name. The New-ZbxRegExp cmdlet sends regexp.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new global regular expression back with regexp.get and writes it. The server requires -Name and -Expression; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a global regular expression

```powershell
New-ZbxRegExp -Name 'Application errors' -Expression @{ expression_type = 'MatchesRegex'; expression = '(ERROR|FATAL)' }
```

Creates a global regular expression named Application errors. The command writes the new global regular expression, read back from the server.
